description: Decision making and conditional statements in C

questions.questionText: Which statement is used to execute a block of code only when a condition is true?
questions.explanation: The if statement executes its block only when the specified condition evaluates to true.

questions.questionText: Which keyword is used to specify an alternative block when an if condition is false?
questions.explanation: The else keyword specifies the block that executes when the if condition is false.

questions.questionText: What will be the output? int x = 10; if (x > 5) printf("A"); else printf("B");
questions.explanation: Since x is 10 and 10 > 5 is true, the if block executes and prints A.

questions.questionText: What will be the output? int x = 3; if (x > 5) printf("Yes"); else printf("No");
questions.explanation: The condition x > 5 is false because 3 is not greater than 5, so the else block executes.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is the correct syntax of an if statement in C?
questions.explanation: The standard syntax is if (condition) { statement; }.

questions.questionText: What type of value is considered false in a C conditional expression?
questions.explanation: In C, zero represents false, while any non-zero value represents true.

questions.questionText: What type of value is considered true in a C conditional expression?
questions.explanation: In C, any non-zero value is treated as true in a conditional expression.

questions.questionText: What will be the output? int x = 0; if (x) printf("True"); else printf("False");
questions.explanation: The value of x is 0, which is treated as false, so the else block executes.

questions.questionText: Which statement is useful when there are multiple conditions to check one after another?
questions.explanation: An else-if ladder is commonly used to check multiple conditions sequentially.

questions.questionText: What will be the output? int x = 15; if (x > 20) printf("A"); else if (x > 10) printf("B"); else printf("C");
questions.explanation: x > 20 is false, but x > 10 is true, so B is printed.

questions.questionText: What is a nested if statement?
questions.optionA: An if statement without a condition
questions.optionB: An if statement with multiple else blocks
questions.optionC: An if statement inside a loop only
questions.optionD: An if statement used inside another if statement
questions.explanation: A nested if is an if statement placed inside another if or else block.

questions.questionText: What will be the output? int x = 10; if (x > 5) { if (x < 15) printf("Yes"); }
questions.explanation: Both conditions are true: 10 > 5 and 10 < 15. Therefore Yes is printed.

questions.questionText: Which operator represents logical AND in C?
questions.explanation: The && operator is the logical AND operator. Both conditions must be true for the result to be true.

questions.questionText: What will be the result of the expression (5 > 3) && (10 > 8)?
questions.explanation: Both conditions are true, so logical AND produces 1.

questions.questionText: Which operator represents logical OR in C?
questions.explanation: The || operator is the logical OR operator. It is true when at least one condition is true.

questions.questionText: What will be the result of the expression (5 > 10) || (8 > 3)?
questions.explanation: The first condition is false but the second condition is true. Therefore logical OR produces 1.

questions.questionText: Which operator is used for logical NOT in C?
questions.explanation: The ! operator performs logical NOT and reverses the truth value of an expression.

questions.questionText: What is the result of !(5 > 3)?
questions.explanation: 5 > 3 is true, represented by 1. Applying ! to true gives false, represented by 0.

questions.questionText: Which statement is commonly used for multi-way selection based on the value of an expression?
questions.explanation: The switch statement allows selection among multiple blocks based on the value of an expression.

questions.questionText: Which keyword is used to define an individual choice inside a switch statement?
questions.explanation: The case keyword defines a possible value within a switch statement.

questions.questionText: Which keyword is used when none of the case values in a switch statement match?
questions.explanation: The default block executes when none of the case values match the switch expression.

questions.questionText: Which keyword is commonly used to prevent execution from continuing into the next case in a switch statement?
questions.explanation: The break statement exits the switch after the matching case is executed.

questions.questionText: What will be the output? int x = 2; switch (x) { case 1: printf("A"); break; case 2: printf("B"); break; default: printf("C"); }
questions.explanation: The value of x is 2, so case 2 executes and prints B.

questions.questionText: Which operator is known as the conditional or ternary operator in C?
questions.explanation: The ?: operator is called the conditional or ternary operator because it uses three operands.

questions.questionText: What will be the value of x? int a = 10, b = 20; int x = (a > b) ? a : b;
questions.explanation: Since a > b is false, the conditional operator selects b, whose value is 20.
